title: Correct metering for mixed-precision batched model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are observing sporadic token-count mismatches in production when requests are routed into mixed-precision/memory-optimized model variants during batching. Symptoms manifest as underbilling on some sessions and overbilling on others, correlated with on-the-fly variant selection (fp16/int8) and dynamic kernel paths. This ticket investigates root causes and implements a deterministic accounting surface so that token attribution is correct regardless of quantization or mixed-precision execution paths.

Problem details: The serving runtime may rewrite requests for a compatible variant (quantized or lower-precision) to save cost/latency. When a batch contains heterogeneous precision variants, two sources of divergence occur: 1) the tokenization->kernel path sometimes applies a lightweight post-tokenization trimming when switching to an int8 execution path which changes counted tokens; 2) internal prefix caching and KV-cache warmup code records prefix lengths per model-id but not per model-variant, causing later finalization to attribute output tokens to the wrong variant or drop small suffix tokens. Both lead to incorrect per-tenant token tallies.

Goal: Make metering invariant to runtime model variant selection and mixed-precision batching. Ensure the metering pipeline captures canonical token counts and a provenance chain that maps final output tokens back to the original request and the exact execution variant for auditing and billing adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical token counts for mixed-precision batched requests match ground-truth offline tokenizer at 1000 simulated sessions with various prefix/suffix patterns
End-to-end e2e test showing no net billing delta when routing identical workloads between float32, fp16, and int8 variants
Telemetry added: per-request token_delta and variant_provenance fields are emitted and searchable in console for post-hoc audits
No more underbilling/overbilling alerts for the sampled customer cohort over a 72-hour Canary window
Documentation updated: operator runbook describing how to reconcile historical invoices if a discrepancy is detected
implementation_notes: Add variant-aware tokenization checkpoints immediately after the tokenizer stage and before any precision-specific rewrites
Emit a stable token_hash and canonical_token_length as part of the metering message payload so downstream aggregators can compare across paths
Refactor KV-cache warmup metadata to be indexed by model_variant_id in addition to model_id; avoid falling back to model_id-only keys
Introduce a tiny deterministic post-processor that normalizes trimming rules across int8/fp16/fp32 to ensure token-length semantic parity
Update billing pipeline schema to include variant_id and a provenance_token_delta for retroactive audits; make schema additions backward-compatible
Performance consideration: canonicalization must add <=0.5ms p99 on the hot path; if overhead exceeds, move canonicalizer to a fast async augment step but preserve strong idempotence guarantees
qa_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer covering edge cases: multi-byte Unicode, control characters, attachment markers, function-call tokens
Integration test harness that replays production traces through fp32/fp16/int8 variant selection and asserts identical canonical_token_length
Canary rollout: 5% of Dedicated capacity with mirrored accounting (new vs legacy) and automated rollback if discrepancy > 0.1% for 12h
Create a synthetic customer scenario that exercises prefix reuse, KV warmup, and a mid-stream variant switch to validate finalization correctness
Post-deploy: run a reconciliation job between telemetry and invoice ledger for affected tenant subset and surface diffs in a dashboard
updates: 2026-02-11: Initial investigation confirmed correlation between variant selection and token_delta spikes. Reproduced locally with a fuzzed batcher that mixes fp16/int8 models.
2026-02-14: PoC canonicalizer implemented in a sidecar process. Benchmarked p95 overhead at 0.35ms but p99 ~0.9ms when run synchronously; need async option.

2026-02-16: Design review with runtime team and billing. Agreed to emit variant_id in metering records and to index KV-warmup metadata by variant_id. Billing agreed to accept schema extension for retro audits.
2026-02-20: Bench tests revealed a corner-case: attachment markers cause tokenizer to emit different token boundaries under int8 post-processing. Added normalization rule for attachments.
2026-02-24: GH PR #7821 opened with canonicalizer and variant_id tagging. Integration tests failing intermittently on non-deterministic trimming behavior; under investigation.

2026-02-28: Fixed trimming nondeterminism by aligning the trimming algorithm to a single, deterministic codepath and added 2000 fuzzed tests. Preparing canary manifest for 5% rollout. Next: coordinate with billing to monitor canary metrics.
